Play-Doh was invented to clean wallpaper.
In the 1930s, homes were heated with coal, and the soot turned wallpaper black.
A soap company in Cincinnati made a soft, squishy putty you rolled across the walls to pick up the dirt.
But then, homes switched to cleaner heating, and nobody needed it anymore.
The company was about to go under.
Then a nursery school teacher, Kay Zufall, noticed kids using the putty to make shapes.
She told her brother-in-law, Joe McVicker, who worked at the company.
They removed the cleaning chemicals, added colors, and she even came up with the name.
Play-Doh has since sold billions of cans. All thanks to dirty wallpaper.
